Lawrence Brittain

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Against all odds the rower who got silver at Rio

Summary:
Cancer survivor Lawrence Brittain bagged a silver medal with his partner Shaun Keeling in rowing at the Rio Olympics. Lawrence defied all odds with an incredible comeback.

Further information:
Brittain had been partners with Shaun Keeling before in the men’s heavyweight coxless pair, but in 2013 his performance started tailing off and was dropped ahead of the 2013 world championships. But it was not his performance that was the problem.
The following year Lawrence was tragically diagnosed with Hodgkin’s disease, a form of lymph-node cancer, in October 2014, after Brittain had felt fatigued and under the weather for months. It actually turned out he had already been living with the condition for two years but it had gone unnoticed.
Lawrence: “The normal symptoms — you’re normally tired, but as an athlete you’re always tired,”

It was his mother Danielle, the team doctor who diagnosed the lymphoma in 2014. She advised him to stop rowing, stop competing and commit to the chemo. He said right and followed the doctors, the perfect patient,. again on his mothers advice he took it on as a battle determined to win
Lawrence: “Finding out [I had cancer] was probably the hardest part. It was such a shock. As an athlete you often have setbacks — injury or falling ill — but this was normal to the extreme.”

Lawrence underwent six 3-week cycles of chemo. In his words without the support of his family, girlfriend and friends he’s not sure if he would have stayed strong.

It was six months before Lawrence was able to rejoin his teammates and get back in a boat. The cardiologist gave him the all clear telling him t go and win medals. Once again he and Shawn were rowing partners.

Shawn: “ He was back in the boat in March, I mean he was tubby and pale and he had no hair, but he was doing his thing to get himself back in his game and get healthy again. “

From a gentle start, when he was told not to push his heart rate above 120 as he exercised gingerly on the training bike, so the workload increased and the challenges mounted. Even the hair grew back, with photos coming back from training camp showing Brittain in hirsute splendour, all mad curls and big ’burns.
While training for the Olympics, he was asked how he was feeling after the cancer:
“I am feeling amazing at the moment. I only started my return to rowing a year ago on last year’s March camp, so I have come a long way.”
“I am stronger than I have ever been, pulling personal bests in all the training and trials, and I keep getting faster without the cancer keeping me back.”

A story of Lawrence’s personal triumph, we tell the back story of his Olympic comeback, talking to Lawrence’s mother, girlfriend and rowing mates.

Press Release:


From Cancer to Olympic Glory
When South African rowers Lawrence Brittain and Shaun Keeling won silver at the Rio Olympics in August this year they were on top of the world. Who would believe that only two years ago Lawrence was told that he had a rare and advanced form of lymph cancer? Carte Blanche meets the heroic young sportsman who fought such turbulent waters and emerged victorious.


Script:


Lawrence Brittain – The Come back Kid

V/O 8 sec
When South African rowers Lawrence Brittain and Shaun Keeling won silver at the Rio Olympics in August… they were on top of the world.

Shaun Keeling I don’t have words to explain how amazing it is to get it….you can see hit the water and Lawrence is going berserk with his hands in the air

Devi: You’re still on an Olympic high?
Lawrence: I think I will never come down from it…I just went up a level and now I am going to stay there


Danielle : It was so emotional I was just crying and couldn’t stop.

V/O 6 sec
Dr Danielle Lincoln wears two hats she’s Lawrence’s mother and the South African rowing team’s doctor.

Danielle: …It was not just him winning silver it was almost like he won gold this was his journey and I know that this is what he always wanted and he was always destined for that.

LINK
Rowing is in Lawrence’s blood. His father David rowed for SA and all four of the Brittain brothers have made their mark in this sport.

Devi What was it like growing up in a highly competitive family?
Lawrence: Crazy so much fun … we had so much fun played so much sport together and was always competitive against each other
Devi: That included your dad?
Lawrence: Definitely my dad is no 1 instigator .

V/O 8 and a half sec
In 96 David Brittain trained for the Atlanta Olympics, he never made the team, but his dedication to the training left it’s mark.

David: Mathew who was 5 when I started training for the Olympics was exposed to that and I suppose it brought some of the drama home got him excited..
Lawrence:…The only time I wanted to row was when Matt started he started because of my Dad and then he was having so much fun.

V/O 9 sec
At the London Olympics in 2012, Mathew the eldest, was part of the men’s lightweight fours rowing team that surged to victory winning gold.

Lawrence I saw him doing well and thought he’s training really hard but it’s not something I cant do he s winning medals and winning gold then I can do the same

V/O 5 sec
Lawrence and Shaun meanwhile were on their own rowing journey, as a heavyweight pair.

Lawrence: The pair is quiet a weird boat because its just you 2 and you each control half the boat and you cannot do it without the other person, you have to b e 100% together…such good friends it’s that bit extra a good mate going just as hard.

Link
2014 was a difficult year after being placed 5th at the World Championships Lawrence’s rowing times began to plateau and Danielle suspected something was seriously wrong.

Danielle: Never anything abnormal or really bad, he was tired all the time so always a bit of a question mark in my mind what’s happening tried to discuss with my husband he would say there is no way he could be rowing at this level and be sick.

Shaun He was doing his best but he was struggling, every time we went overseas Lawrie kept on getting sick and we just couldn’t understand why.

Lawrence: it was up and down I always believed there was no limit to how fast I could be if I trained a little harder I can get 1 sec faster and at that point I was not getting the seconds so it was really tough not getting the results that you want.

V/O 12 sec
In October 2014 Lawrence was diagnosed with Hodgkin’s disease a rare form of lymph cancer, Stage 4. The very field David as a clinical haematologist worked in.

Up Sound…all the other black stuff is cancer…..

Devi: It’s one thing when it’s a patient but another when it’s your child?
Its hugely different even now I get a cold shiver in my spine and a huge know in my stomach when I think back to that time its terrible

Danielle It was just so emotional I said Lawrence will be ok I believed that I never believed he wouldn’t be ok

V/O 6 AND A HALF sec
Less than a week later Lawrence started the first of six three week cycles of chemotherapy.

Lawrence Ya I think cancer attacks body so hard need mental strength to be able to fight sickness and just sickness not how fat or bald I was getting just about getting better

Devi: You refused to treat your son?
David: Its different when its your son remember there is no such thing as a free lunch and everything you do has a consequence so to many tests too many antibiotics too much chemo can be just as bad a too little and so I fortunate magnificent team of people with me and I could be a parent, a normal worried anxious dad not a dr who didn’t know how to make a decision because he didn’t know where he stood.

V/O 7 AND A HALFsec
Six weeks after he started chemo the scan was clear. Lawrence was allowed to start training slowly building up his strength.

Shaun: He was tubby and pale no hair but he was doing his thing just trying to do his thing trying to get healthy again. …

Devi: At what point did Rio real in your head
…I need to get back to crew boat I’d just been rowing the crew boat he said you are still to fat to row with everyone else.
Devi: He said it just like that
Lawrence: Straight out no beating around the bush for our team, they team went off to Italy for tour I was ok fat no1 I’m going on mega diet

V/O 9 AND A HALF
Six months after getting back in the boat, Lawrence and Shaun qualified for the Olympics…six months after that they were at Rio in the men’s pair final.

Devi: What is it about his character that made him come back like that?
David: He’s incredible stubborn from when he was a child he would not do something he didn’t want to do if he wanted to do something you couldn’t stop him.

Up Sound

Shawn I gave him a punch and said this is awesome that we are doing this together and no matter what happens I am really glad we have had a good ride and lets just give it our best and be happy with what we get

Lawrence: When I got on to start line at the Olympics that was crazy that was when it all became real..

David: I kept saying the result does not matter because the fact that he is well and here is special enough
Lawrence: We struggled a little bit through the middle
David: the NZ came through them Italians were through them and then the British were through them I thought WOW you cant come back from a quality field like this that you are losing ground on.
Lawrence …..but once we had moved on Italy and GB the podium was on the cards we knew it was happening.
David: I said they are coming back and they are going to get the silver,
Lawrence: We were ridiculously strong at the end there and we knew we were going to be on the podium in the last 100 m UP SOUND bring the line here this is going to be awesome 4 sec Its something you dream about from Grade 8 it out did all the expectations ..it really was some thing special
